column2: Skeptics of the exploding-mic theory put this clip up themselves: a real shaped charge detonating into a large smoke cloud that is absent from the event footage. Proponents answer that a micro-charge is not a breaching charge.
The transport Yukon was reportedly towed, cleaned and put on a path to resale rather than sealed as a forensic surface. Auto carpet holds residue well, and no interior panel has ever been published.

Stew Peters states that he was the one who tied the exploding-mic theory to the AES defense order, two weeks before the plant blew up. The page records his claim and asks readers to help check the dates.

Building 602 in McEwen, Tennessee went up on October 10, 2025 with roughly 24,000 pounds of material inside, and sixteen workers were killed. It happened a month after the killing and weeks after researchers named the plant.

On the contract's delivery date a private aircraft flew Heber City to the airport nearest the AES plant, and logged no return leg. The flight and the contract are verifiable; the inference that they connect is a theory.

The fork that moves the device off the chest and into the ear canal — low-flash fill, wire whip, an RF or voltage trigger. It answers the smoke objection at the cost of needing an entirely different custody list.
A line reportedly caught on a 911 call from the vehicle: "get that off of him." The clip is unverified and the poster does not say what "that" was — which is exactly why it keeps circulating.

Not every exploding-mic post means military fill. This fork argues the transmitter's own lithium-polymer cell went into thermal runaway — a different failure, and a completely different list of things a lab would look for.

The SEAL who shot Osama bin Laden and a brigadier general reviewed the footage on NEWSMAX and said independently that something exploded on him. Eyeball judgement rather than lab work, but not anonymous.

Six visual signatures — refraction at the microphone, a pre-wound flinch, absent cavitation, radial fabric expansion, the necklace's final position — argued as things a rifle round cannot produce. The author's reading, reproduced near-verbatim.

A C-32A Air Force Two airframe logged into Las Vegas on May 27, 2025, three and a half months before the killing. It sits in the catalogue as an open question about a VIP movement, not as an allegation against anyone.

The Army ISR jet that flew near campus did not lift off from a civilian executive terminal. It reportedly departed an active Army airfield at Fort Bliss, and that military origin is the detail investigators keep returning to.

One base links the government jet that flew west before September 10 and the aircraft that carried the casket the day after. The page also separates the two tail numbers people keep confusing, 99-0404 and 99-0004.

The Utah Air National Guard base beside Salt Lake City International, where Air Force Two received the casket on September 11. A documented, respectful transport, recorded for the record rather than for suspicion.
Air Force Two carried the casket from Salt Lake City to Phoenix on September 11, with the Vice President aboard. It is the one flight in this section that nobody disputes.

Commentary alleges the Utah governor held back-to-back closed-door meetings with Egyptian and French figures thirteen days after the killing. The page records the claim and states plainly that no wrongdoing by any official or diplomat has been shown.
A tip reportedly from inside the booking process places the occupants of the Egyptian jets in one named Orem hotel from September 4. Folios and camera servers could settle it in a week.

Erika Kirk invited the public to check the logs of N102DZ; researchers say the tracking history came off FlightRadar24 in May 2026. Owners block tails for ordinary privacy reasons all the time, which is why the page keeps both readings.

The biggest allegation in the aircraft angle: that foreign government jets overlapped TPUSA travel for years and tightened in the final two months. The overlap counts disagree with each other, and the page shows exactly where.

What intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance aviation actually does, and why a contractor structure keeps crews and tasking orders out of public reach. Read it before judging any single ADS-B track.

The Israel thread of the aircraft angle — jets that trackers say went dark over the eastern Mediterranean and reappeared on Israel legs. Parts of that routing are documented and parts are inferred, and the page marks which is which.
The Kirk family aircraft, reported flying Scottsdale into the Salt Lake City area on the morning of September 10. It matters because it anchors where the party was in the hours before the event.

The fleet sister of the N1098L spy plane — same operator, same Global 6500 airframe, same Army reconnaissance work. It has never been placed over campus, and researchers disagree about whether it belongs in the case at all.

A six-seat Beechcraft logged into Provo on September 10, listed so that no arrival that day goes uncounted. Nothing in the public record ties this aircraft, its crew or its passengers to the shooting.
John Cullen calls this the gorilla in the room next to the N1098L elephant. Public reporting on the tail is thin, so the page records it as a lead worth pulling records on rather than a finding.

A Citation XLS that flew a short Scottsdale, Provo and Santa Barbara out-and-back on the morning of September 10, flagged on air by Candace Owens. The reported owner is described as a donor aviation entity; nothing beyond the route is established.

A tail described in commentary as one TPUSA insiders used, named in the draft disclosure laws over a reported October 2025 Fort Huachuca to Kalispell leg. Standalone sourcing is thin, and naming an aircraft accuses nobody.

A Piper Navajo configured for high-resolution camera and LiDAR mapping reportedly flew four survey passes over campus hours before the shooting. What it photographed, and who tasked it, has never been established.
One of the Provo arrivals on September 10, thin on its own, but sharing a Santa Barbara origin with N560TW and with a disputed tarmac timeline. Clusters are how thin leads become checkable ones.

The weakest-sourced aircraft entry on the site: a turboprop reportedly seen circling near campus, with no tail number and no flight track at all. It is catalogued so the claim is logged and clearly caveated.

The working memo for the aircraft angle — ISR passes, the Egyptian fleet, shadowing counts, SAM movements and transponder gaps, each with the record that would settle it. Start here if you want the questions rather than the tails.

One of three callsign readings reported for the same government VIP airframe around the Fort Huachuca window. The page exists so the identifier stays searchable and the uncertainty is stated rather than smoothed over.

Another reported callsign for tail 99-0404 in the September 8–9 window, listed in the source notes as one of three possible readings. Keeping each identifier separate is how a bad reading gets caught.

A Special Air Mission callsign that surfaces in pre-event route tracking through Andrews, Nashville and Colorado Springs. It is tied to no confirmed tail in the case notes, which is why it is catalogued rather than argued.

A C-37A Gulfstream tracked into Fort Huachuca two days before the shooting, tied by an anonymous tipster to a reported meeting of about twelve lieutenant colonels. The flight is public record; the meeting is not.
The fifth tail in the armada researchers count through Provo, and the one with the least written about it. Its weight comes entirely from the fleet pattern, not from any single documented event.
One of the five Egyptian-registered jets in the Provo cluster, with almost no standalone reporting behind it. John Cullen's maintenance-contract explanation is set out beside the shadowing reading.
A Falcon 7X counted in the armada that is rarely discussed on its own. The page is candid that its significance is membership in a pattern, and gives the maintenance-contract counterpoint room.

The minute-by-minute aviation timeline for September 10 — the transponder window, the afternoon arrival, the hospital timing conflict. It is where the aircraft claims either line up with the clock or fail to.
Two more foreign tails flagged when the Egypt story grew from two jets to five. Route detail is thin; they appear in the source notes grouped simply as more planes for disclosure.

How the story was framed in the first hours — the descriptions that spread instantly and the ones that quietly went away. The section asks why a wound description can be everywhere on television and nowhere in the footage.

Early dispatch called the roof figure all black; later materials associate the charged defendant with jeans, a hat and sunglasses. The page keeps the radio layer, the ground-witness layer and the roof video separate, because threads online collapse all three into one claim.

This branch of the skepticism does not deny that someone was on the roof. It denies that the person fired, reading the bag, the prone pause and the missing assembly footage as theater while the harm came from nearer the stage.

Commentators say the figure sprints, drops, then crawls sideways several feet into a prone position, and that the motion reads as trained. The honest counter is that a short compressed clip cannot carry that much inference.

Citizen reviewers say dark figures appear on the Woodbury, Sorensen and Sparks roofs the same morning, not only on Losee. If any of that holds, the single-perch geometry stops being the only geometry.

Posts circulating with the July 2026 roof footage say the prone figure flashed a bright object moments before the public shot time. Whether that was an optic, a phone, or nothing at all decides whether anyone was being signalled.

A sixteen-to-twenty-foot drop taken with no pause at the edge, no scouting of the corner and no fumbling of the carried object. Sam Parker calls that rehearsal; the fair counter is that a short clip can flatter ordinary panic.

The victim, the widow and the accused, with the questions that orbit each role. It is where the death-threat messages, the 12:23 call and the TPUSA succession dispute sit on one page instead of three.

One man reportedly shouted that he was the shooter and was cleared within hours; another was announced in custody and released about ninety minutes later. Neither was charged, and that is exactly what the page is about.

The people who claim direct sensory contact with the shot or the shooter — a construction electrician who described a figure in black, a front-row witness who heard a pop rather than a rifle crack, a videographer reportedly told to delete his 4K footage.
Almost everything the public knows about this case was surfaced by people with no badge. This page names them and records what each one actually contributed, without treating any of them as suspects.

The surgeons, the medical examiner, the defense counsel and the prosecutors — several of whom took their posts in the weeks before September 10. The page logs the timing coincidences citizen investigators raise and declines to call them proof.
Who controlled the narrative, the custody clock and the foreign-lead follow-up. It indexes roles rather than verdicts: every official named here is alive, public, and accused of nothing.

The SUV detail and the campus police were the only protection layer in the courtyard. What they saw, which cameras they controlled, and why the rooftop reportedly went uninspected are the questions that stay open.

The most-quoted medical claim in the entire case has no named source. Every version of the "it should have gone through" story routes through one spokesman and an anonymous doctor. The strange part is not what was said — it is that no name has ever surfaced.

A passenger name that exists only inside unverified flight notes attached to an Egyptian-registered jet into Provo. This site records that the name circulates; it endorses nothing and alleges nothing. Read it as a study in how a name enters an investigation.

A Utah surgeon whose name sits on an unverified list of seven names that commentators say were queried from abroad. The allegation is about who reportedly searched — not about anything the doctors did. No authority has adopted the list.

A PragerU personality named among reported attendees of the August 2025 Bridgehampton gathering. His own on-record recollection has Charlie Kirk complaining about "moral blackmail" during an argument over Israel. Reported attendance is context here, never an accusation.

The Israeli prime minister's son, named in commentary as a reported attendee of a July 31, 2025 White House session that Charlie Kirk and TPUSA reportedly missed. Hamptons presence claims about him are unverified commentary only. No investigation has connected him to September 10.

A pro-Israel advocacy figure listed among reported attendees of the July 31, 2025 strategy session where TPUSA was reportedly absent. That meeting preceded the Hamptons intervention by about four days. Presence at a meeting is not evidence of anything beyond presence.

Named publicly only as a brother in the Qureshi family, with a thinner record than almost anyone else on this site. An unverified note — flagged "NEED TO DOUBLE CHECK" — puts a Qureshi brother on drones at Fort Huachuca. Whether it refers to him at all is unknown.

Egypt's sitting president enters this investigation only through an anonymous post that lined up routine diplomatic calls and asked whether they were coincidence or collusion. The commentary is a series of leading questions, not evidence. It is kept here as a record of how speculation travels.
